challenges.title: TLS Provenance Fabrication
challenges.problem: Negotiated group/signature algorithm values were fabricated from experiment configuration rather than derived from actual observation.
challenges.investigation: Forensic review (P4-002) found normalize_tls_event() accepted configuration values, violating provenance requirement (PRD §8.1, architecture.md §3.5).
challenges.resolution: normalize_tls_event() now takes only NegotiationObservation; configuration never consulted; unobserved fields = null.

challenges.title: W1 Controlled-Abort Semantics
challenges.problem: W1 workload was completing full handshakes then mislabeling as aborted_pre_finished.
challenges.investigation: State machine analysis showed openssl s_client -brief with timeout was not reliably aborting pre-Finished.
challenges.resolution: Implemented do_handshake_on_connect=False with non-blocking socket; completed handshake raises (→ error), never aborted_pre_finished.

challenges.title: Packet Capture Lifecycle
challenges.problem: tcpdump capture blocked indefinitely; no explicit start/stop; timeout used as normal termination mechanism.
challenges.investigation: Blocking capture process could not be cleanly stopped; failed captures returned zero bytes silently.
challenges.resolution: start_packet_capture()/stop_packet_capture() with SIGINT; timeout = emergency backstop only; cleanup on both success and failure; failed = unavailable not zero.

challenges.title: Controller Integration
challenges.problem: CPU/bytes fabricated as constants; missing measurements reported as zero; TLS events config-derived.
challenges.investigation: Integration testing revealed result schema violations: measurement_status missing, null-not-zero not enforced.
challenges.resolution: Full null-not-zero schema; measurement_status per stream (measured|unavailable|failed); provenance-locked TLS events; zero-attempts guarded.

challenges.title: CPU PID Ambiguity
challenges.problem: Shell wrapper process matched 'openssl s_server' in /proc/*/cmdline, causing pidstat to sample wrong PID.
challenges.investigation: ps -ef inside container showed both shell wrapper and actual openssl process; /proc/*/cmdline inspection required.
challenges.resolution: Require exact 'openssl' executable + 's_server' in args; reject shell wrappers; verified at runtime (P4-003).

challenges.title: Custom SSL_stateless() Server Abandoned
challenges.problem: Custom C/OpenSSL SSL_stateless() server consistently failed with SSL_R_INTERNAL_ERROR in tls_construct_stoc_cookie for ML-KEM-768 (both 3.5.5 and 3.5.9).
challenges.investigation: Extended debugging of cookie callback implementation; OpenSSL internal error during stateless cookie construction for PQ groups.
challenges.resolution: Abandoned custom server; adopted openssl s_server -stateless CLI path which empirically produces HRR via key-share mismatch.

challenges.title: D1 Cookie Scope Corrected — HRR Without Cookie
challenges.problem: The intended stateless HRR-cookie defense (RFC 8446 §4.2.2) was not realized for ML-KEM-768.
challenges.investigation: Manual openssl s_client -msg -state transcript analysis in Docker lab with OpenSSL 3.5.9 confirmed: HRR special random observed, MLKEM768 key_share requested, ClientHello2 with MLKEM768 key_share, ServerHello completed — but cookie extension (type 44) absent in HRR and ClientHello2.
challenges.resolution: Documented as measured outcome: D1 = HRR without cookie for ML-KEM-768; cookie_observed=false is legitimate measured data, not missing data. RQ4/RQ5 evaluated with measured implementation.

challenges.title: Phase B Validation — Separate Capture Window
challenges.problem: W1 aborts pre-Finished, so ClientHello2/ServerHello never occur in W1 capture window; RTT parser returns null.
challenges.investigation: D1 validation requires observing full forced-HRR flow (CH→HRR→CH2→SH), but W1 by definition aborts early.
challenges.resolution: Added separate bounded D1 validation phase (Phase B) that runs full TLS 1.3 handshakes against D1 server in dedicated pcap window before W1 measurement (Phase A). Phase B excluded from all W1 denominators.

challenges.title: In-Network Client Addressing
challenges.problem: Legitimate client ran on host with Python ssl (OpenSSL 3.0.21, cannot negotiate ML-KEM-768) targeting Docker service name 'tls-server' (unresolvable from host).
challenges.investigation: Host Python OpenSSL too old for PQ; Docker service names only resolve inside lab network.
challenges.resolution: Clients requiring lab service resolution run INSIDE lab network via docker exec with OpenSSL 3.5.x; host used only for orchestration/readiness on 127.0.0.1:<published port>.

challenges.title: Phase 6 ML-KEM Keypair Reuse Not Implemented
challenges.problem: openssl s_client does not support reusing a pre-generated ML-KEM keypair across connections via CLI.
challenges.investigation: OpenSSL 3.5+ s_client generates fresh keypair per connection; no CLI mechanism to inject pre-generated keypair. True reuse requires custom C client using OpenSSL API directly.
challenges.resolution: Documented fallback to fresh keypair per attempt in both 'fresh' and 'reused' conditions. Null result on server-side cost difference reflects fresh keypairs in both cases. RQ3 remains unresolved for true keypair reuse.

challenges.title: RTT Extraction Limitation
challenges.problem: Packet-capture RTT parsing implemented for Phase 7 validation only; main campaign reports wall-clock latency only.
challenges.investigation: TLS handshake message parsing from pcap for RTT counting (1 RTT vs 2 RTT) requires reliable message identification; implemented for D1 validation phase.
challenges.resolution: RTT available for D1 validation (2 RTT observed for HRR path); not available for main Phase 5/6 campaign. Wall-clock p50/p95 reported instead.
